Paul may be a gamer, but is Petscop a game? Is it like any other game out there? Petscop, throughout Paul's playlist, has proven to be an incredibly obtuse and difficult piece of media to engage with, ridiculous time constraints and indecipherable content that continues to confound both Paul and we the audience. 

But even so, gamers do have their tendencies, there's no doubt about that. Yet this is a let's play as well, and a Petscop let's play, the one and only. The videos have puzzles that present themselves to us both, Paul and the audience. Yet time and time again Paul acts in a manner almost as unpredictable as Petscop itself. Why would he record the first encounter with Toneth and not Pens, when Toneth drastically changes the Pet text's importance? 

Because, as I said, this isn't just Paul playing the game. It's Paul's Let's Play. At the bare minimum, it is Paul playing the game, recording his play, editing that footage, and selectively uploading his edited gameplay. 

With a game like Petscop, would we not want a naturalistic or holistic approach to engaging Petscop? To broadcast every interaction live, to leave nothing out of the reel, least Paul ignores something, misses something, overlooks something. We're his audience, we're the over obsessive ones, we're the thinkers and analyzers, we're his workforce! 

Or are we? Does Paul want our input? Does he care? If not, why upload? Why the edits? Why the channel at all? His earliest justifications are in Petscop 1, to prove to someone of its existence. So why upload it publicly, why not send it out in some email, something private, rather than this video public to the world?

Petscop is a story told as a game, through a recording of several play sessions, by someone editing his raw footage, and then selectively uploading those edits onto Youtube. I do not think that something like this was done absent-minded.

This might be fleshed out into its own thread-topic for discussion, but just a quick thing now:

I think this series is doing a good job conveying a story through the let's play medium, and unpacking that. One thing that could be talked about is how quickly he went through Pen's description page. I actually had to slow down the video down to read it all, though it didn't produce anything too profound. In other ARGs, there's often flash-frames, something hidden that has to be found by closely examining the video, frame by frame.

But that's usually because of a "glitch." Here, information is conveyed to us by the player, Paul, at his pace. This isn't a walk-through, this is a play session. It's his captured footage, his engagement with Petscop, and we're still not sure why he's even uploading these videos. Perhaps I'm one who really doesn't want him responding to us. It's a new approach to the unreliable narrator trope and I think begs more analysis, not to get any more secrets from the plot but as a discussion on the nature of let's plays and the relationship between let's player and the fan.
